lean.statement: ∀ {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [CompleteSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] (mu : Measure E) {eta : ℝ}, eta ≠ 0 → ∀ y y' x : E, gradient (fun t => -(‖t - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta)) - Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (-(‖z - y‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))) ∂mu) - (-(‖t - y'‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))) + Real.log (∫ z, Real.exp (-(‖z - y'‖ ^ 2 / (2 * eta))) ∂mu)) x = eta⁻¹ • (y - y')
approved_definition_context: gradient is the Hilbert-space representative of the Fréchet derivative and is totalized outside differentiability; the theorem proves the displayed function genuinely has the stated derivative.
The integral terms in the displayed function are scalar constants with respect to the variable t.
Real inversion is totalized, while the explicit eta nonzero premise permits the usual field simplification.
No Borel-space compatibility is required by this purely spatial calculus identity.
